title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from the previous page). X is a space with a locally finite stratification indexed by a poset I. The strata are X_i^*, and the closed strata are X_i = ∪_{i'≤i} X_{i'}^* (this is (Strat 3)). 'Fidèle' means X_i ⊂ X_j ⇔ i ≤ j. 'Dense' presumably means X_j is the closure of X_j^*. For J ⊂ I, X_J^* = ∪_{j∈J} X_j^*.

(1) Top of the page. Assume density and faithfulness. Give I the Alexandrov-type topology in which closed sets are the down-closed subsets (i ≤ j means 'i lies in the closure of j'). Then X_L^* is open in X iff L is open, i.e. up-closed. For any J, the closure of X_J^* is X^*_{\bar J}, where \bar J is the down-closure of J, so \bar{X_J^*} \ X_J^* = X^*_{\bar J \ J}. Hence X_J^* is locally closed iff \bar J \ J is closed in I, i.e. iff J is locally closed (convex). Grothendieck calls such a J a 'bande'. In modern terms, X → I is a continuous map to a poset with its Alexandrov topology, and under density plus faithfulness it is a quotient map whose open sets are exactly the up-sets.

(2) (94). For each i, V_i = V(X_i^*, X) is a chosen 'regular' or tubular-type open neighbourhood of the stratum X_i^* in X. The inclusion X_i^* ↪ V_i is a homotopy equivalence, with a side remark that seems to involve X metrisable.

(3) (95). V_i ∩ X_j^* ≠ ∅ ⇔ V_i ∩ \bar{X_j^*} ≠ ∅ ⇔ X_i^* ∩ \bar{X_j^*} ≠ ∅ ⇒ X_i^* ∩ X_j ≠ ∅ ⇒ i ≤ j.
- The first equivalence holds because V_i is open.
- The second holds for V_i small enough: by local finiteness, X_i^* has a neighbourhood missing every closed set \bar{X_j^*} that does not meet it.
- The third implication is an equivalence under density.
- The last is an equivalence under faithfulness.
So for a dense faithful stratification, V_i ∩ X_j^* ≠ ∅ ⇔ i ≤ j: the tube of stratum i meets stratum j iff i lies in the closure of j. Grothendieck stresses that this relation is not symmetric in (i, j).

(4) (96). In contrast, after a suitable shrinking (he invokes metrisability), V_i ∩ V_j ≠ ∅ ⇒ i and j are comparable. The converse holds for faithful stratifications. This is the familiar control-data condition on tubes (tubes of incomparable strata are disjoint).

(5) (97). He defines V_ij = V_i ∩ V_j. This is the start of the 'déploiement': in the intended theory V_ij (i<j) should be the deleted tube, homotopy equivalent to the link or homotopy link of X_i^* in X_j^*. The construction then proceeds to chains i_0<…<i_n, i.e. a diagram of spaces over the flags of I that reconstructs X up to homotopy.
errors: The equivalence V_i∩\bar{X_j^*}≠∅ ⇔ X_i^*∩\bar{X_j^*}≠∅ is not automatic for an arbitrary neighbourhood V_i. It requires choosing V_i small enough (local finiteness plus closedness of the relevant strata closures). The page leaves this implicit.

(96) likewise needs a coherent shrinking of all the V_i (as in Mather's control data). It is not true for arbitrary homotopy-equivalent neighbourhoods. Grothendieck flags this only by a marginal 'si X métrisable'.
In (95), the converse labelled 'équiv. si strat. fid.' (i≤j ⇒ X_i^*∩X_j≠∅) also tacitly needs X_i^* ≠ ∅.

ideas.what: Stratification as a continuous map to a poset with its Alexandrov topology; X_L^* open iff L up-closed, X_J^* locally closed iff J convex ('bande')
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; formalised in Lurie, Higher Algebra, Appendix A.5 (2017)

ideas.what: Neighbourhoods V_i of the strata with X_i^* ↪ V_i a homotopy equivalence; V_i meets X_j^* iff i ≤ j; V_i ∩ V_j ≠ ∅ only for comparable i, j
ideas.modern_name: Tubular neighbourhoods / control data (Thom–Mather); regular neighbourhoods
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 discusses tubular neighbourhoods and the 'dévissage' of stratified structures in general terms

ideas.what: Intersections V_ij = V_i ∩ V_j as building blocks of the 'déploiement' (unfolding of a stratified space into a diagram over chains of I)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quinn (homotopically stratified sets, 1988); MacPherson, Treumann, Lurie (exit paths)

missed.claim: The page begins a combinatorial-topological construction of the 'déploiement' via the pairwise tube intersections V_ij. The notes end shortly afterwards (page 94 of 98), so the full unfolding over flags is not carried out here. The idea itself is well represented in later homotopy-link and exit-path theory.
missed.quote: On posera (97) V_{ij} déf= V_i ∩ V_j
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only historical: it documents Grothendieck's 1981–82 route toward what became the exit-path / homotopy-link picture. No new mathematics beyond what is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is standard point-set bookkeeping for stratified spaces: the Alexandrov-topology correspondence and tube-intersection conditions familiar from Thom–Mather control data. Its interest is historical, as a step toward the 'déploiement' sketched in the Esquisse; it contains no unknown result.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 likely reads 'sous[?] hypothèse de densité et fidélité, ...', not 'et seulement[?] densité et fidélité'.
'Dans le cas = hypothèses' is likely 'Dans les mêmes hypothèses' (or 'Sous les mêmes hypothèses').
The note under the hook arrow in (94) reads 'équiv. d'homotopie (X métrisable, ...)', not 'X unités'. The symbol over the arrow is likely '(h)' or '(≃)'.
In (95) the labels belong under the arrows: 'équiv. si strat. dense' under the first ⇒ and 'équiv. si strat. fid.' under the second ⇒.

The word after 'V_i' in 'Soit maintenant, pour tout i∈I, V_i le pro…' is uncertain; it denotes a neighbourhood (V for voisinage), possibly 'le voisinage' or a word beginning 'pro…', not clearly 'prolongement'.
The marginal annotation over (96) appears to read 'si X métrisable, dans le[s] ... [convenablement choisis]'.
The sentence before (96) is roughly: 'On fera attention que cette relation n'est pas symétrique en (i,j), contrairement à [celle] qui s'exprime par : V_i∩V_j≠∅.'
